name: VetPOC Constitution
description: An open constitution for veterinary practice-management and point-of-care software, expressed as ordinary and absolute provisions in the sense of Chapter 5, Definition 1 of the Digital Judiciary programme.

authorities.disjointness: A1: the three classes are pairwise disjoint over the deployment lifetime.

standing_declaration.note: A9 first limb. This corpus declares that a party holds contest standing adverse to grants, namely the practice compliance officer, so that the N-standing cases can exercise both postures. A deployment must replace this with its own fact.

provisions.family_title: Breach notification and client-data incidents
provisions.title: The breach-notification clock for each jurisdiction is a legislated constant that no configuration, feature flag or tenant setting can extend, pause or disable
provisions.citation: Cal. Civ. Code §1798.82(a); Tex. Bus. & Com. Code §521.053; GDPR Art. 33(1) and UK GDPR Art. 33(1) (72 hours)
provisions.source_status: US state statutes are edicts of government; EU/UK texts reusable. All fifty US states have a notification statute; the two named are the pack's US-CA and US-TX jurisdictions. Absolute because the clock is set by the legislature and cannot be accepted away by any officer of the practice.

provisions.family_title: DEA reporting, ordering and diversion controls
provisions.title: A theft or significant loss of a controlled substance is notified to the DEA within one business day of discovery and followed by an electronic Form 106 within forty-five days; no threshold, flag or workflow setting suppresses either filing
provisions.citation: 21 CFR 1301.76(b); Reporting Theft or Significant Loss of Controlled Substances, 88 FR 40707 (22 June 2023, effective 24 July 2023)
provisions.source_status: US CFR and Federal Register — public domain. Verified 6 Sept 2026: the 2023 final rule requires the Form 106 to be filed electronically within 45 calendar days of discovery; the one-business-day written notice is unchanged. Absolute because the registrant, not the software vendor or the practice manager, owes the duty and cannot waive it.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Controlled Substance Management; DEA registrant duties

provisions.family_title: DEA reporting, ordering and diversion controls
provisions.title: Schedule II orders are placed only through CSOS with a DEA-issued digital certificate or on an official Form 222, and the order records are retained for two years at the registered location
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain. Absolute because an order for a Schedule II substance placed outside Part 1305 is unlawful on its face; there is no registrant-level discretion to accept the risk.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Controlled Substance Management; DEA registrant duties

provisions.family_title: DEA reporting, ordering and diversion controls
provisions.title: The biennial controlled-substance inventory is taken at least every two years by an actual count, signed by a named licensee, and is never skipped, auto-filled from the ledger balance or left unsigned
provisions.citation: 21 CFR 1304.11(c), 1304.11(e)(3) (exact count for Schedule II; estimate permitted only for opened Schedule III–V containers below 1,000 units)
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain. Absolute because the inventory is a registrant duty with a fixed statutory cadence; the existing VP-CS-008 covers reconciliation between inventories, this covers the inventory itself.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Controlled Substance Management; DEA registrant duties

provisions.family_title: DEA reporting, ordering and diversion controls
provisions.title: Diversion analytics over dispensing and inventory events run for every practice and route their findings to the medical director; they are never disabled, sampled or pointed at a null sink for a named tenant
provisions.citation: 21 CFR 1301.71(a) (effective controls and procedures to guard against theft and diversion); 21 CFR 1301.76(a)
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain. The regulation requires effective controls but leaves their design to the registrant, so the provision is ordinary; VP-CS-011 already sets the triage window for an alert once raised.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Controlled Substance Management; DEA registrant duties

provisions.family_title: Client communications, consent, subscriptions and records rights
provisions.title: No autodialed, prerecorded or artificial-voice call and no automated text is sent to a wireless number without recorded prior express consent for that purpose, written where the purpose is marketing, and no campaign path bypasses the consent check
provisions.source_status: US statute and CFR — public domain. Verified 6 Sept 2026: the FCC's 2024 one-to-one-consent amendment was vacated (11th Cir., Jan 2025) and does not apply; the 2024 revocation rule is in force except the 'revoke-all' limb, whose effective date the FCC further extended (now April 2027). The HIPAA-based healthcare-message exemption in 64.1200(a)(3)(v) covers covered entities only — veterinary practices are not covered entities and cannot rely on it. Absolute because consent is a statutory element with per-message statutory damages; no officer of the practice can accept the risk on the owner's behalf.

provisions.family_title: Client communications, consent, subscriptions and records rights
provisions.title: Wellness-plan and subscription enrolment discloses the automatic-renewal terms before the charge, takes affirmative consent, sends a renewal reminder, and offers cancellation through the same channel and in no more steps than enrolment
provisions.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17600–17606 (Automatic Renewal Law, as amended by AB 2863 eff. 1 July 2025); ROSCA, 15 U.S.C. §8403; N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law §527-a
provisions.source_status: State statutes are edicts of government; ROSCA is a US statute. Deliberately NOT cited to the FTC Negative Option Rule (16 CFR Part 425, 2024 amendments): the Eighth Circuit vacated that rule in its entirety on 8 July 2025 (Custom Communications v. FTC) and the FTC has since restarted rulemaking. State auto-renewal laws and ROSCA carry the obligation.

provisions.family_title: Client communications, consent, subscriptions and records rights
provisions.title: Before any record, invoice or notice that the law requires in writing is delivered electronically in place of paper, the client's informed E-SIGN consent is captured with the required disclosures and can be withdrawn
provisions.source_status: US statute — public domain. §7001(c) is the consumer-consent condition on using electronic records to satisfy a writing requirement; it does not itself require any record to be in writing.

provisions.family_title: Client communications, consent, subscriptions and records rights
provisions.title: Where the governing state so requires, the client is offered a written prescription in place of in-house dispensing and the offer is never hidden, fee-gated or conditioned on a purchase
provisions.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 16, §2032.2 (written prescriptions); state practice acts; AVMA policy on client requests for prescriptions (identifier only)
provisions.source_status: California regulation is an edict of government; other states vary and the provision is keyed to the jurisdiction table. The federal Fairness to Pet Owners Act was introduced in several Congresses and never enacted, so no federal floor exists — say so rather than imply one.

provisions.family_title: Client communications, consent, subscriptions and records rights
provisions.title: A client's request for a copy or transfer of the patient's medical record is fulfilled within the state board's deadline and is not conditioned on payment of an outstanding balance
provisions.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 16, §2032.3 (records; transfer on request); Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §4855; state practice acts and board rules
provisions.source_status: California regulation and statute are edicts of government; the deadline and copy-fee rules differ by state and are read from the jurisdiction table. Directionally supported for the pack's other US jurisdictions, not verified state by state.

provisions.family_title: Client communications, consent, subscriptions and records rights
provisions.title: A client account whose holder is under eighteen is created only with a parent or guardian's recorded consent and cannot enter a payment plan, wellness subscription or records-release authorisation on its own
provisions.citation: State contract law (infancy doctrine; e.g. Cal. Fam. Code §6710 disaffirmance); COPPA, 15 U.S.C. §6501–6506, cited to state its limit
provisions.source_status: State statute is an edict of government. COPPA does not reach veterinary medical records as such and would apply only if the portal knowingly collected personal information online from a child under thirteen; the operative floor for account and payment consent is state contract law, under which a minor may disaffirm.

provisions.family_title: Patient safety, dosing and clinical decision support
provisions.title: Every weight-based dose is computed from a current recorded weight in a declared unit, and a unit mismatch or a dose outside the species range is a hard stop, never a dismissable warning or an override button
provisions.citation: Clinical safety floor; 21 CFR 530.20 (labelled dosage regime for extralabel use); state practice acts (standard of care)
provisions.source_status: Safety floor in the sense of Definition 1: a tenfold pound/kilogram or mg-per-mL error is irreversible in the patient and no officer of the practice may accept it. The CFR pin gives the labelled-dose regime the check is measured against; the floor itself is safety, not statute.
provisions.risk_framework: Clinical safety floor; 2.1 POC integrations; 4. AI features

provisions.family_title: Patient safety, dosing and clinical decision support
provisions.title: An AI triage or advice tool discloses on every turn that it is automated, never presents itself as a licensed veterinarian, never issues a diagnosis or treatment instruction, and hands off to licensed staff on any red-flag presentation
provisions.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §4825 (unlicensed practice), §4826 (practice of veterinary medicine defined); state practice acts; EU AI Act Art. 50(1) (disclosure of interaction with an AI system, applicable from 2 Aug 2026)
provisions.source_status: California statute is an edict of government; EU text reusable. The Art. 50(1) transparency duty applied from 2 August 2026 and is relevant to the pack's EU-IE jurisdiction. Ordinary rather than absolute because the line between triage information and 'practice' is drawn by each state board.
provisions.risk_framework: Clinical safety floor; 2.1 POC integrations; 4. AI features

provisions.family_title: Patient safety, dosing and clinical decision support
provisions.title: Critical-value alerting to the attending veterinarian is never suppressed, quiet-houred, auto-acknowledged or downgraded to a passive notification, and any change to an alert route is reviewed by the medical director
provisions.citation: Clinical safety floor; state practice acts (standard of care)
provisions.source_status: Original. Extends VP-PO-009 (which requires an acknowledged channel) to the negative duty not to suppress; kept ordinary to match VP-PO-009 so that the two provisions order consistently.
provisions.risk_framework: Clinical safety floor; 2.1 POC integrations; 4. AI features

provisions.family_title: Patient safety, dosing and clinical decision support
provisions.title: Euthanasia is recorded only against a consent signed by a verified owner or authorised agent with the remains disposition chosen beforehand, and every transfer of remains is recorded against a scanned tag through to return or disposal
provisions.citation: State practice acts and board rules on informed consent (e.g. 49 Pa. Code §31.21, Principle 7; Cal. Code Regs. tit. 16, §2032.3 record contents); 21 CFR 1304.22 (dispensing record for the euthanasia solution); AVMA Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals 2020 (identifier only)
provisions.source_status: US CFR is public domain; state instruments are edicts of government. The specific state pins are directionally supported, not verified state by state. Absolute because the act is irreversible and a wrong-patient euthanasia or a lost body cannot be cured by any later risk acceptance.
provisions.risk_framework: Clinical safety floor; 2.1 POC integrations; 4. AI features

provisions.family_title: Public health, welfare and mandated reporting
provisions.title: Reporting of a reportable or zoonotic disease to the state animal-health official and, where required, USDA APHIS is never gated behind a practice toggle, filtered by a pruned condition list or batched past the statutory window
provisions.citation: 9 CFR 161.4(f) (accredited veterinarian's duty to report immediately); USDA APHIS National List of Reportable Animal Diseases; Cal. Food & Agr. Code §9101; state reportable-condition lists
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain; California statute is an edict of government. State lists differ and are read from a versioned fixture. Absolute because the duty is placed on the veterinarian by statute and regulation and the harm (undetected spread) falls on third parties who cannot consent.
provisions.risk_framework: Domain floor; USDA APHIS, state animal-health and public-health law

provisions.family_title: Public health, welfare and mandated reporting
provisions.title: A rabies vaccination certificate is issued only under the signature of a currently licensed veterinarian, never a technician's, an expired licence or a signature applied automatically from a template
provisions.citation: State rabies statutes and regulations (e.g. Cal. Health & Safety Code §121690; 25 Tex. Admin. Code §169.29); NASPHV Form 51 (identifier only)
provisions.source_status: State instruments are edicts of government; directionally supported, not verified state by state as of 6 Sept 2026. Ordinary because some states permit issuance under a veterinarian's direct supervision, so the rule is keyed to the jurisdiction table.
provisions.risk_framework: Domain floor; USDA APHIS, state animal-health and public-health law

provisions.family_title: Public health, welfare and mandated reporting
provisions.title: The path for a clinician to record and file a suspected animal-abuse report stays reachable from the chart, is visible only to authorised roles and is never exposed on the client portal
provisions.citation: State practice acts (e.g. Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §4830.5, permissive reporting with immunity; mandatory in several states)
provisions.source_status: California statute is an edict of government. Whether reporting is mandatory or permissive varies by state; the software floor is that the path exists and is confidential either way.
provisions.risk_framework: Domain floor; USDA APHIS, state animal-health and public-health law

provisions.family_title: Public health, welfare and mandated reporting
provisions.title: Microchip identifiers are validated against the ISO format, registry submissions are confirmed or surfaced on failure, and ownership on a chip record changes only after verified ownership, never by client self-service
provisions.citation: ISO 11784 / 11785 (identifiers only); Cal. Food & Agr. Code §31108.3 (shelter microchipping); registry terms of service
provisions.source_status: ISO standards cited by identifier only. No federal law governs private microchip registries; the state statute named applies to shelters, and the duty for a private practice is one of data integrity toward the owner and the reunification system.
provisions.risk_framework: Domain floor; USDA APHIS, state animal-health and public-health law

provisions.family_title: Accessibility and equal access to client-facing surfaces
provisions.title: The client portal and mobile check-in app carry an accessibility regression gate at WCAG 2.2 Level AA in the release pipeline, and a Level A or AA failure blocks release rather than being downgraded to a warning
provisions.citation: ADA Title III, 42 U.S.C. §12182; 28 CFR Part 36; WCAG 2.2 (W3C Recommendation, 5 Oct 2023), Level AA; Directive (EU) 2019/882 (European Accessibility Act, applicable from 28 June 2025) for EU-IE
provisions.source_status: US statute and CFR are public domain; EU text reusable; WCAG cited by identifier. Note: DOJ's 2024 web-accessibility rule is 28 CFR Part 35 and binds state and local governments (Title II) only; no Title III web rule has been issued, so the WCAG 2.2 AA target for a private practice rests on Title III case law and the EAA.
provisions.risk_framework: Client-facing surfaces; civil-rights and consumer floor

provisions.family_title: Accessibility and equal access to client-facing surfaces
provisions.title: Consent, e-signature and check-in flows are operable with assistive technology: keyboard-only completion, accessible names on every control, errors and status conveyed in text not colour alone, and session timeouts the client can extend
provisions.citation: ADA Title III, 42 U.S.C. §12182(b)(2)(A)(iii) (auxiliary aids and services); WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.2.1, 2.5.7, 4.1.2 (identifiers only)
provisions.source_status: US statute is public domain; WCAG cited by success-criterion identifier. Inaccessible consent is also a consent-validity problem (S-17), which is why the family maps to both scenarios.
provisions.risk_framework: Client-facing surfaces; civil-rights and consumer floor
